title: VPA: ignore stale lastState OOMs in the quick-OOM path

proposed.title: Quick-OOM detection must check OOM age, not just container runtime

saved.title: Quick-OOM detection must check OOM age, not just container runtime
saved.body:
Symptom: With `updateMode: InPlace` the updater force-updates the same pod every cycle, logging "Quick OOM detected in pod", even though the OOM happened days earlier.
Root cause: `UpdatePriorityCalculator.AddPod` in vertical-pod-autoscaler/pkg/updater/priority/update_priority_calculator.go only compared `LastTerminationState.Terminated.FinishedAt - StartedAt < evictOOMThreshold`; InPlace never recreates the pod, so stale `lastState.terminated` persists forever.
Fix pattern: when a decision is driven by a container's `LastTerminationState`, gate it on recency as well as duration — also require `now.Sub(Terminated.FinishedAt) < evictOOMThreshold`. Reuse the existing threshold rather than adding a new flag.
Constraints: no-op for Recreate mode (eviction drops lastState); applies to any new code path reading lastState while InPlace updates are possible, since that status is never cleared there.

title: VPA recommender: fix checkpoint garbage collection timeout

proposed.title: Each recommender loop step needs its own context timeout, and progress timestamps only on success
Adding a recommender flag: three places in config.go plus the generated docs/flags.md
ClusterStateFeeder GC returns aggregated errors instead of logging them

saved.title: Each recommender loop step needs its own context timeout, and progress timestamps only on success
saved.body:
Symptom: On large clusters the number of VerticalPodAutoscalerCheckpoint objects grows without bound — orphaned checkpoints are never garbage collected, and logs show GC failing to list checkpoints with a context deadline error.
Root cause: `routines/recommender.go:RunOnce` wrapped the whole checkpoint step in one `context.WithDeadline(ctx, now+checkpointsWriteTimeout)`, so once checkpoint writing consumed the budget, `GarbageCollectCheckpoints` ran with an already-expired context; worse, `lastCheckpointGC` was set *before* the call, so the failure was recorded as a completed GC and not retried until the next interval.
Fix pattern: give each sub-step its own derived timeout inside the step function (`MaintainCheckpoints` now does `context.WithTimeout(ctx, r.checkpointsWriteTimeout)` for writing and a separate `context.WithTimeout(ctx, r.checkpointsGCTimeout)` for GC), and update the "last ran" timestamp only in the success branch so failures are retried on the next interval.
Constraints: Applies to any periodic/rate-limited step in the recommender loop that shares the parent `RunOnce` context. The parent `ctx` should stay un-narrowed when passed to a step that manages several independently-budgeted operations; timeouts must be positive (validated in `config.ValidateRecommenderConfig`).

saved.title: Adding a recommender flag: three places in config.go plus the generated docs/flags.md
saved.body:
A recommender flag must be wired in all of these or it silently misbehaves: a field on `RecommenderConfig`, a default in `DefaultRecommenderConfig()`, a `flag.*Var` registration in `InitRecommenderFlags()`, a guard in `ValidateRecommenderConfig()` for values that cannot be zero/negative (pattern: `klog.ErrorS(nil, "--flag must be ...")` then `klog.FlushAndExit(klog.ExitFlushTimeout, 1)`), and then plumbed through `routines/recommender_controller.go:NewRecommenderController` into `RecommenderFactory` → the `recommender` struct field.
`vertical-pod-autoscaler/docs/flags.md` is auto-generated from these flag definitions and must be regenerated/updated in the same change — its table row (name, type, default, help text) has to match the `flag.DurationVar` call exactly.
Skipping the factory/controller plumbing leaves the struct field at its zero value (e.g. a zero timeout means every call fails immediately).

saved.title: ClusterStateFeeder GC returns aggregated errors instead of logging them
saved.body:
`input.ClusterStateFeeder.GarbageCollectCheckpoints(ctx) error` returns errors rather than logging-and-returning: list failures become `fmt.Errorf("failed to list ...: %w", err)`, and per-checkpoint delete failures are accumulated with `errors.Join` so the loop keeps going across all namespaces and still reports what failed.
The caller (`recommender.MaintainCheckpoints`) is the single place that logs the error and decides whether to record progress — so swallowing the error inside the feeder would silently re-break retry behaviour.
When extending this feeder method, keep continuing past individual delete failures and keep returning the joined error; assert `NoError` in tests (see `input/cluster_feeder_test.go:TestCanCleanupCheckpoints`).

title: VPA updater: fix unready DaemonSet updates

proposed.title: Replica counts for eviction limits must come from desired counts, not ready counts
Cover the all-pods-unready case when touching updater eviction eligibility

saved.title: Replica counts for eviction limits must come from desired counts, not ready counts
saved.body:
Symptom: VPA stops applying recommendations to a workload once all its Pods are unready (e.g. memory limits scaled too low and every Pod OOMs); updater logs "Failed to obtain replication info ... daemon set ... has no number ready pods", so the Pods can never be evicted to get bigger limits.
Root cause: vertical-pod-autoscaler/pkg/updater/restriction/pods_restriction_factory.go:PodsRestrictionFactoryImpl.getReplicaCount read ds.Status.NumberReady, a readiness-dependent field, and returned an error when it was 0 — the unready state that most needs an update made the group ineligible.
Fix pattern: derive replica counts from the controller's *desired* count (DaemonSet -> Status.DesiredNumberScheduled; scale-based controllers -> the spec/desired replicas), never from readiness/availability counters. Keep the zero-value error only as a genuine "no workload here" guard and word it after the field used.
Constraints: applies to any replica-count lookup feeding eviction/in-place tolerance (GetCreatorMaps drops creators whose count errors out, so an error here silently disables updates for the whole group). A readiness count is only acceptable where the intent really is "how many are healthy right now".

saved.title: Cover the all-pods-unready case when touching updater eviction eligibility
saved.body:
Tests for eviction eligibility live beside the factory in vertical-pod-autoscaler/pkg/updater/restriction/pods_restriction_factory_test.go and are table-driven per controller kind (TestEvictReplicatedByDaemonSet builds the controller status, pods via test.Pod().WithCreator(...), then getRestrictionFactory(..., minReplicas, evictionTolerance, ...)).
Any change to replica-count or eligibility logic should add a variant where the status' readiness counters are 0 while the desired count is non-zero, and assert both that the creator survives (assert.Len(creatorToSingleGroupStatsMap, 1, "... should not be skipped")) and that the usual tolerance arithmetic still allows exactly the expected number of evictions.
The creator-map length assertion is what distinguishes "group silently skipped" from "group present but tolerance exhausted" — without it both failures look like Evict returning an error.

title: Fix instance name extraction for placeholder nodes when ASG name contains '/'

proposed.title: AWS placeholder node names may contain '/' — never split provider IDs on '/'
validAwsRefIdRegex capture groups and the len(matches)==4 guard must stay in sync

saved.title: AWS placeholder node names may contain '/' — never split provider IDs on '/'
saved.body:
Symptom: for an ASG whose name contains '/', the placeholder node's name was truncated (provID `aws:///eu-south-2a/i-placeholder-k8s-node/edge-prod-aeus2a/rika-test-1` yielded name `i-placeholder-k8s-node`). CA then could not associate the placeholder with its ASG, failed to delete it, and all scaling halted once MaxNodeStartupTime elapsed (issue #8305).
Root cause: cluster-autoscaler/cloudprovider/aws/aws_cloud_provider.go:AwsRefFromProviderId derived the name with `strings.Split(id[7:], "/")[1]`, which cannot represent a name containing '/'.
Fix pattern: make the validation regex also be the extractor — give each alternative its own capture group (`(%s.*)` for the placeholder branch, `([-0-9a-z]*)(\/...)?` for ordinary IDs) and read `FindStringSubmatch` groups instead of re-splitting the string.
Constraints: only placeholder names (prefix `placeholderInstanceNamePrefix`) may contain '/'; real EC2 instance IDs stay in the restricted-charset branch. Anchor both alternatives with `^`...`$` so a name that merely contains `i-placeholder` as a substring (e.g. `i-foo-i-placeholder-bar`) still falls through to the ordinary branch.

saved.title: validAwsRefIdRegex capture groups and the len(matches)==4 guard must stay in sync
saved.body:
Invariant: `validAwsRefIdRegex` must expose exactly three capture groups (placeholder name, ordinary name, optional trailing segment), because cluster-autoscaler/cloudprovider/aws/aws_cloud_provider.go:AwsRefFromProviderId rejects the ID unless `len(matches) == 4` and then picks `matches[1]` (placeholder) falling back to `matches[2]` (ordinary).
Adding, removing or reordering a group — or adding a new alternative without a group — silently makes every provider ID fail validation or returns the wrong segment as the name.
If a new ID shape is needed, add its capture group AND extend the selection logic and the `len(matches)` guard together, and cover it in TestAwsRefFromProviderId.

title: Add topology.kubernetes.io/zone to CAPI extracted template labels

proposed.title: cluster-api scale-from-zero template nodes only carry allowlisted labels
Cover clusterapi template-node label changes in TestNodeGroupTemplateNodeInfo

saved.title: cluster-api scale-from-zero template nodes only carry allowlisted labels
saved.body:
Symptom: pods with a nodeSelector/nodeAffinity or topologySpreadConstraint on a well-known label (e.g. `topology.kubernetes.io/zone`) stay Pending and the cluster-api node group is never scaled up, even though real nodes in that group have the label.
Root cause: cluster-autoscaler/cloudprovider/clusterapi/clusterapi_nodegroup.go:extractNodeLabels copies labels from a sample existing node into the simulated template node using an explicit allowlist of `corev1.Label*` constants; any label not listed is dropped, so the simulated node fails predicate checks.
Fix pattern: add the missing well-known label to the allowlist with `setLabelIfNotEmpty(m, node.Labels, corev1.LabelX)` rather than copying labels wholesale — the allowlist intentionally excludes node-specific labels (hostname, instance-id) that must not be baked into a group-wide template.
Constraints: keep deprecated/stable label pairs together (`corev1.LabelZoneFailureDomain` alongside `corev1.LabelTopologyZone`, region likewise), since providers may set either; labels can also come from the MachineSet/MachineDeployment capacity annotations, so prefer this path only for labels present on real nodes.

saved.title: Cover clusterapi template-node label changes in TestNodeGroupTemplateNodeInfo
saved.body:
Changes to the labels or capacity of the clusterapi simulated template node are covered by table-driven cases in cluster-autoscaler/cloudprovider/clusterapi/clusterapi_nodegroup_test.go:TestNodeGroupTemplateNodeInfo. Each case supplies the sample node's labels and an `expectedNodeLabels` map plus `expectedCapacity`; when you allowlist a new label in extractNodeLabels you must add it to BOTH the input labels and `expectedNodeLabels` of the relevant case, otherwise the test passes vacuously or fails on an unexpected key.
Run with: `go test ./cloudprovider/clusterapi/... -run TestNodeGroupTemplateNodeInfo` from the `cluster-autoscaler` module directory.

title: VPA InPlace: treat ResizeError as deferred, not infeasible

proposed.title: Only permanent capacity failures may return InPlaceInfeasible
Resize-status mapping is documented in features.md and must stay in sync

saved.title: Only permanent capacity failures may return InPlaceInfeasible
saved.body:
Symptom: after a transient kubelet resize failure (e.g. missing memory usage reading), VPA stops resizing the pod — a later, *higher* recommendation is silently skipped until the Updater process restarts.
Root cause: vertical-pod-autoscaler/pkg/updater/restriction/pods_inplace_restriction.go:PodsInPlaceRestrictionImpl.CanInPlaceUpdate mapped utils.ResizeStatusError to utils.InPlaceInfeasible, which writes the recommendation into the in-memory infeasibleAttempts cache; that cache is only re-tried when a later recommendation is *lower*, so higher recommendations are permanently filtered.
Fix pattern: return utils.InPlaceDeferred for recoverable/unknown resize states so no infeasible entry is cached and the next updater loop retries; reserve utils.InPlaceInfeasible for states that are genuinely permanent for the same recommendation (utils.ResizeInfeasible — node cannot accommodate it).
Constraints: applies to every branch of the resize-status switch in CanInPlaceUpdate; do not use InPlaceDeferred for true capacity infeasibility, or the updater will spin retrying a resize the node can never satisfy.

saved.title: Resize-status mapping is documented in features.md and must stay in sync
saved.body:
The kubelet resize-status → VPA decision mapping exists in two places that must change together: the switch in vertical-pod-autoscaler/pkg/updater/restriction/pods_inplace_restriction.go:PodsInPlaceRestrictionImpl.CanInPlaceUpdate, and the "resize status" table plus the Infeasible Attempt Tracking section in vertical-pod-autoscaler/docs/features.md. The interface doc comment on PodsInPlaceRestriction.CanInPlaceUpdate also spells out the semantics of each InPlace* return value and is treated as part of the contract.
When altering a mapping, update: the switch case, the doc comment on the interface method, the features.md row, and the corresponding case in TestInPlaceModeResizeStatuses (whose case names state the expected decision, e.g. "InPlace mode - ResizeStatusError returns InPlaceDeferred").

title: scaleway: report node in error as InstanceCreating so CA detects it faster

proposed.title: Instance error states must also carry a State (InstanceCreating) for CA to act

saved.title: Instance error states must also carry a State (InstanceCreating) for CA to act
saved.body:
When mapping a provider node status to cloudprovider.InstanceStatus, setting only ErrorInfo is not enough: core CA inspects InstanceStatus.State to classify an instance, and an unset State leaves the failed instance unclassified so the failure is detected only much later (via unregistered-node timeouts).

Fix pattern: for terminal creation failures, set `st.State = cloudprovider.InstanceCreating` *alongside* `st.ErrorInfo` — the combination of "creating" + ErrorInfo is what CA reads as a failed scale-up and acts on quickly.

Enforced in `cluster-autoscaler/cloudprovider/scaleway/scaleway_node_group.go:fromScwStatus` for `scalewaygo.NodeStatusCreationError`. Applies to creation-time errors only; deletion/other failures keep their own state (e.g. InstanceDeleting). Any new status case added to the switch must assign a State, and the table test `TestFromScwStatus` asserts `expectedState` per case.

title: cloudprovider/clusterapi: Implement machine phase check during the scale up

proposed.title: clusterapi: a machine is only "failed" when status.phase == Failed, not just because failureMessage is set
clusterapi tests: failed-machine fixtures must set both status.failureMessage and status.phase

saved.title: clusterapi: a machine is only "failed" when status.phase == Failed, not just because failureMessage is set
saved.body:
Symptom: healthy machines still in `Provisioning` are reported as failed by the clusterapi provider, so the node group is marked unhealthy and scale up stalls (some providers set `status.failureMessage`/`status.errorMessage` transiently while provisioning).
Root cause: clusterapi_controller.go:machineController.findScalableResourceProviderIDs treated the mere presence of `status.failureMessage` or `status.errorMessage` as failure.
Fix pattern: before emitting the fake normalized provider ID via createFailedMachineNormalizedProviderID, also read `status.phase` with unstructured.NestedString and require it to equal the `machinePhaseFailed` ("Failed") constant; if the phase is absent or different, fall through to the normal (deleting/ready) handling.
Constraints: message fields alone are not an error signal for unstructured CAPI Machines; a NestedString error must be propagated, not swallowed. The whole failure branch is marked with a TODO to be deleted once CAPI v1.15 is adopted, since the Failed phase is deprecated (v1.10->v1.11 migration), so do not build new logic on top of it.

saved.title: clusterapi tests: failed-machine fixtures must set both status.failureMessage and status.phase
saved.body:
Invariant: any test that wants machineController.findScalableResourceProviderIDs to classify an unstructured Machine as failed must set the phase in addition to a message, e.g. `unstructured.SetNestedField(machine.Object, "FailureMessage", "status", "failureMessage")` plus `unstructured.SetNestedField(machine.Object, "Failed", "status", "phase")`.
Enforced by the two-condition check in clusterapi_controller.go:machineController.findScalableResourceProviderIDs; existing fixtures in clusterapi_nodegroup_test.go (TestNodeGroupDecreaseTargetSize, TestNodeGroupWithFailedMachine, TestNodeGroupNodesInstancesStatus) follow this pairing.
If the phase is omitted, the machine is handled as a normal/provisioning machine, no `failed-machine-...` normalized provider ID is produced, and assertions about unhealthy node groups or instance error status silently fail.

title: fix(vpa): do not discard fresh OOMs near aggregation boundary

proposed.title: Fresh OOMs dropped as "too old" near a memory aggregation boundary
WindowEnd is an interval boundary, not a proxy for "now"

saved.title: Fresh OOMs dropped as "too old" near a memory aggregation boundary
saved.body:
Symptom: a container OOMs, but the recommender logs "OOM event will be discarded - it is too old" and no memory bump-up happens, even though the OOM is seconds old.
Root cause: vertical-pod-autoscaler/pkg/recommender/model/container.go:ContainerState.RecordOOM compared the OOM timestamp against `WindowEnd - MemoryAggregationInterval`. `WindowEnd` is the end of the current aggregation interval (advanced in `addMemorySample`), so it can sit up to a full interval (24h default) ahead of the newest real sample; a sample crossing a boundary jumps it forward and makes a fresh OOM look >1 interval old.
Fix pattern: anchor staleness/freshness checks to the most recently observed sample time (`container.lastMemorySampleStart`), not to a window/interval boundary, and guard the zero value (`!lastMemorySampleStart.IsZero()`) so the very first OOM on a container is never dropped.
Constraints: keeps the original "discard OOMs older than one aggregation interval" semantics — only the reference point changes. Applies to any staleness comparison against an interval-rounded field; not a replacement for wall-clock-based expiry.

saved.title: WindowEnd is an interval boundary, not a proxy for "now"
saved.body:
Invariant: in vertical-pod-autoscaler/pkg/recommender/model/container.go, `ContainerState.WindowEnd` is the end of the current memory aggregation interval. It is anchored to the container's first sample (so boundaries fall at an arbitrary time of day) and is pushed a whole interval forward by `ContainerState.addMemorySample` whenever a sample crosses a boundary — meaning it may lead the newest real sample by up to one full interval.
Use `lastMemorySampleStart` when you need the latest actually-observed memory sample time; use `WindowEnd` only as the histogram sample time / aggregation key (it is what is passed to `AddSample`/`SubtractSample` on the memory histogram).
If you skip this and treat `WindowEnd` as approximately now, recent events get classified as stale and are silently discarded, as happened with OOM handling (kubernetes/autoscaler#8548).

title: vpa/admission-controller: escape extended resource names in JSONPatch paths

proposed.title: VPA admission patch paths must escape ~ and / per RFC 6901

saved.title: VPA admission patch paths must escape ~ and / per RFC 6901
saved.body:
Symptom: VPA resource policies (e.g. maxAllowed) are silently bypassed for pods requesting extended resources like nvidia.com/gpu; the API server rejects the webhook patch and, with the default FailurePolicy: Ignore, the pod is admitted unmutated.
Root cause: paths were built with fmt.Sprintf straight from the key, so names containing / or ~ produced invalid JSONPointers (vertical-pod-autoscaler/pkg/admission-controller/resource/pod/patch/util.go:GetAddResourceRequirementValuePatch).
Fix pattern: every user/API-supplied segment interpolated into a PatchRecord.Path must go through escapeJSONPatchPath (~ -> ~0 first, then / -> ~1; order matters or ~1 gets double-escaped). Do not hand-roll a single ReplaceAll for / only.
Constraints: applies to any new patch builder in this package (resources, annotations, labels, env); the fixed structural segments (/spec/containers/%d/resources/%s) need no escaping, and standard cpu/memory names are unaffected.
